terms.storyLine: A whole work, owned by you and handed to a Reader as one link.
terms.sceneLine: A linear run of Shots, and the only unit at which a Story branches.
terms.shotLine: One beat: an image, its text, or both. The smallest thing a Reader is shown.
terms.exitLine: A way on from one Scene to another, offered at the end of a Scene for the Reader to take.
terms.conditionLine: A test that decides whether a Shot plays or an Exit is offered, so the same Scene reads differently without ever branching.

step.heading: Next
step.dismiss: I can take it from here
step.nameScene: Every Story starts with a Scene. Write the first one here: it opens for writing with its name selected, so “The arrival” is the first thing you type.
step.writeShot: A Shot is an Image and its text, as much as the Reader is shown at once. Add one, and write the first thing they read.
step.wayOn: An Exit is the way on, and a Story branches between Scenes rather than inside one. At the foot of this Scene, name the Scene the Exit leads to — a name nothing answers to writes that second Scene, already joined. The Graph draws the two as soon as they are.
step.setFlag: State is what one Reading carries with it. Give this Scene a Flag — “courage = high” — and it is set on every Reader who enters.
step.openingScene: A Reading has to start somewhere, and nothing marks where this Story does. Write a Scene and mark it as the one to start on — any of them will do, and you can name another whenever you like.
step.putCondition: A Condition makes the same Scene play differently to different Readers, without branching. Take a Shot of this Scene, or add one, and have it played only when that Flag holds something else — “low” will do. Nothing plays it yet, which is the point.
step.previewCondition: Nothing plays that Shot, and the reading says why: read the Story on the engine a Reader runs, and it shows what each Shot it skipped asked for beside what the State actually holds. Read that, then put the value right.
step.publish: That is a Story that works. Publish it, and anybody can read it at a link of its own — the one this page then shows, to hand to whoever you wrote it for.

remark.noOpening: This Story marks no opening Scene, so no Reading can start. Mark the Scene it opens on.
remark.sceneUnreached: No Exit arrives at {scene}, and the Story does not open on it, so no Reader ever gets there.
remark.sceneUnplayed: {scene} holds no Shot: a Reader arriving there is shown nothing.
remark.shotUnwritten: Shot {place} of {scene} carries neither text nor Image.
remark.imageUndescribed: The Image of Shot {place} of {scene} has no Description, so a Reader who cannot see it is told nothing about it.
remark.soundUntranscribed: {carrier} has no Transcript, so a Reader who cannot hear it is told nothing about it.
remark.flagUntested: {scene} sets the Flag {flag}, and no Condition anywhere tests it.
remark.flagUnset: A Condition in {scene} tests the Flag {flag}, and no Scene ever sets it.
remark.exitUnofferable: The Exit {place} out of {scene} is offered only when {flag} holds “{is}”, which no Scene ever sets it to.
remark.shotUnplayable: Shot {place} of {scene} plays only when {flag} holds “{is}”, which no Scene ever sets it to.
remark.exitNeverTaken: The Exit {place} out of {scene} leads back to a Scene a Reading arriving here has already been through, so no Reader is ever offered it.

tooManyConditions.shot: A Shot cannot carry more than {max} Conditions.
tooManyConditions.exit: An Exit cannot carry more than {max} Conditions.

refusals.badCondition: A Condition tests what one Flag holds, or whether one Scene has been entered.
refusals.exitTextLong: An Exit cannot carry more than {max} characters.
refusals.exitTarget: An Exit arrives at a Scene.
refusals.exitStepsBack: An Exit is stepped back across, or it is not, or it says as its Story says.
refusals.sceneNameLong: A name cannot be longer than {max} characters.
refusals.tooManyFlags: A Scene cannot set more than {max} Flags.
refusals.badFlag: A Flag is a name and a value, and neither of them may be left empty.
refusals.tooManyFlagValues: A Flag cannot be drawn from more than {max} values.
refusals.flagValueSeparator: A Flag's value cannot hold “{separator}”, which is what separates one value of a draw from the next.
refusals.storyTitleLong: A title cannot be longer than {max} characters.
refusals.storyLanguage: A Story is written in one language.
refusals.storyStepsBack: A Story is stepped back through, or it is not.
refusals.storySynopsisLong: A Synopsis cannot be longer than {max} characters.
refusals.cover: A Cover is one of the Story's own Images.
refusals.shotTextLong: A Shot cannot hold more than {max} characters.
refusals.description: A Description says what an image shows, in at most {max} characters.
refusals.imageMissing: An image is a file to upload.
refusals.imageHeavy: An image cannot weigh more than {mb} MB.
refusals.imageType: A Shot carries a JPEG, a PNG or a WebP image, and nothing else.
refusals.soundMissing: A Sound is a file to upload.
refusals.soundHeavy: A Sound cannot weigh more than {mb} MB.
refusals.soundType: A Sound is an AAC or an MP3 file, and nothing else: those are the two every browser plays.
refusals.transcript: A Transcript says what a Sound makes heard, in at most {max} characters.
refusals.soundLoops: A Scene’s Sound is held in a loop, or it is played once.
refusals.namedSound: A Scene takes its Sound from a Scene of this Story that carries one of its own.
refusals.authorName: A Name is what you appear under, so it cannot be empty.
refusals.authorNameLong: A Name cannot be longer than {max} characters.
refusals.nameBeforeListing: A Story is listed under its Author's Name, so write yours before listing it.
refusals.listPublished: A Story is published before it is listed, because an entry in the Catalogue leads to its public link.
refusals.openingScene: A Story needs an opening Scene before it can be published. Write a Scene on the Graph and mark it as the one to start on.
refusals.signedOut: You are no longer signed in, so nothing was written.
refusals.commentText: A Comment carries what you have to say, so it cannot be empty.
refusals.commentTextLong: A Comment cannot be longer than {max} characters.
refusals.nameBeforeCommenting: A Comment is signed with its Author's Name, so write yours on the list of your own Stories before commenting.
refusals.listTitle: A List gathers Stories under a title, so it cannot be empty.
refusals.listTitleLong: A title cannot be longer than {max} characters.
refusals.favouritesTitle: Favourites is the List every account has, so it has no title to write.
refusals.favouritesDelete: Favourites is the List every account has, so it cannot be deleted.
refusals.split: A Scene is split before one of its own Shots, and never before the first.
refusals.wayBack: A Reading stands in a Scene once, so an Exit cannot lead back to a Scene the Reader may already have come through. Duplicate that Scene, and lead the Exit to the copy.
